lesson.title: Couleur: The Famous Rebel
lesson.subtitle: la couleur, l'erreur, la peur, la chaleur: why abstract Latin -or nouns stayed feminine in French.

hook.title: Why Abstract Qualities in -eur Are Feminine
hook.content: Human professions in -eur are masculine (le docteur, l'acteur), while abstract sensations and natural phenomena in -eur are feminine: la couleur ('color'), l'erreur ('error'), la peur ('fear'), la chaleur ('heat'), and la fleur ('flower')!

footnotes.title: Two exceptions that stayed masculine: le bonheur and l'honneur
footnotes.content: le bonheur ('happiness', built on Latin neuter augurium 'omen') and l'honneur ('honour') are the two non-person -eur words that stayed masculine.

pattern.title: Quality in -eur → Feminine la / une
pattern.content: Pair la couleur, l'erreur, la peur, la chaleur, and la fleur with feminine articles and adjectives (une belle couleur, une grande erreur).
pattern.linguist_note: Gallo-Romance reassigned Latin abstract nouns in -ōrem to the feminine gender.
pattern.trap_note: Don't write *un erreur or *le couleur — both are feminine quality nouns (une erreur, la couleur)!

exercises.prompt: Match each feminine -eur noun with its meaning:
exercises.target_answer: the color, the error / mistake, the fear, the heat / warmth, the flower
exercises.meaning: la couleur, l'erreur (une erreur), la peur, la chaleur, la fleur
exercises.explanation: All five take feminine la / une.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'a beautiful color' in French?
exercises.explanation: couleur is feminine, so both une and belle are feminine!

exercises.prompt: Translate with the indefinite article ('a'): 'a mistake / an error' →

exercises.idea: this color is very beautiful (use Cette couleur)
cues: is very beautiful → est très belle
exercises.explanation: couleur is feminine, triggering Cette and belle.

diagnosis.cue: couleur is feminine: Cette couleur est très belle.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.meaning: It is a pretty red flower
cues: BAGS adj before noun: une jolie fleur
exercises.explanation: jolie stands before fleur; rouge stands after.
exercises.affirmation: You flanked fleur with jolie and rouge accurately.

summary.outcome: Use feminine articles and adjectives with la couleur, l'erreur, la peur, la chaleur, and la fleur.

use_example.german: Quelle belle couleur sur cette fleur !
use_example.english: What a beautiful color on this flower!

summary.takeaway: People in -eur are le; qualities and sensations in -eur are la.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "This color is very beautiful" in French:
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Cette couleur est très belle" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Couleur: The Famous Rebel.

couleur.etymology_derivation: Latin color → couleur — feminine, the famous exception the -eur squad warns you about.

erreur.etymology_derivation: Like la couleur, l'erreur kept its Latin feminine gender from abstract qualities.

peur.context_translation: I am afraid (lit. I have fear).
peur.etymology_derivation: Latin pavor → peur. Feminine abstract noun.

fleur.etymology_derivation: Latin flōrem → French fleur → English flower.

heure.etymology_derivation: Latin hōra. Silent H triggers elision: l'heure.

bon.etymology_derivation: Latin bonus 'good' — English borrowed the word back as 'bonus', a good thing added.

eur.name: The -eur Bridge
eur.phonetic_rule: Latin -or/-er nouns convert to -eur /œʁ/: doctor → docteur, color → couleur.
eur.historical_linguistics: The agent and quality suffixes of Latin split three ways in English (-or, -er, -our) but re-merge in French as -eur.
eur.philological_note: -eur is usually masculine — couleur and erreur are the famous rebels. The lesson names the exceptions before you trust the rule blindly.
